Triage (maintainer-authorized one-off pass, 2026-08-09, registered on #6015): **held as `finding`, routed `domain:metadata`** (was unrouted). Dormant — zero such overlay rows in the corpus (measured at PR #6608), so no stuck operator exists today. Restart conditions: (1) any deployment reports a legacy overlay row it cannot remove (the 403 path here), or (2) #6858's ADR-0094 D5-R revision lands — its ruling on the materialized-layer direction decides whether this delete path gains a legal door or the whole legacy-overlay layer gets an explicit migration story; re-grade then.

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-10, directed in session `session_01BPWqbmEFU8gJepBJTHESXd`): the delete side moves — removal of a legacy env overlay on a rolled-back type is allowed through the ordinary delete path.**

Deleting an overlay restores the code-declared state: it is the narrowing direction and cannot widen anything, so refusing it serves no security purpose while trapping repair behind `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE`. Create and update on such items stay refused exactly as today. Record the asymmetry (delete-only) in the gate's doc so it is not "fixed" into symmetry later. Zero affected rows today — dispatch at normal priority, not urgent.

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

**PM: ruling consumed, card is dispatchable — but it is SEQUENCED behind PR #7306, and that is a same-function conflict, not a formality** (`domain:metadata` seat, session `session_01W6bLax4KMrSfnE1ydFU8Dw`). Recording now so it is not re-derived, and so nobody dispatches it in parallel.

## The collision

The ruling moves the **delete** side: removal of a legacy env overlay on a rolled-back type goes through the ordinary delete path. Per this card's own analysis the refusal lives at exactly two sites:

- `deleteMetaItem`'s `environmentId !== undefined` branch in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (`artifactBacked && !overlayAllowed` → `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403);
- `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`, refusing `override-artifact` on the no-`environmentId` kernel path.

**PR #7306 (ADR-0029 D9, `Fixes #7277`) just added pins to both of those sites, asserting the refusal.** From its own report: *"the same predicate feeds `deleteMetaItem`'s two-tier authorization and `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`, so RESETTING such a customization is refused too — and the repository check is topology-independent, so a control-plane kernel refuses as well. Both are pinned rather than softened (a fixture encoding the old leniency would be encoding the defect)."*

So this card and that PR reach for the same two gates from opposite directions, in the same batch window. The maintainer's standing rule for this lane is explicit — `protocol.ts` region-disjoint parallel authorship is authorized, **same function / same region never in the same batch**. This is the same function. It waits.

## The part that needs a ruling, and it is NOT a contradiction

The two are not actually in conflict on substance, and I want that on the record before anyone reads #7306's pins as blocking this ruling:

- **#7306 / D9.6 pins the `object` case** — an overlay write over a *packaged* object, where the refusal is the ratified design and the reset refusal is its declared (and flagged) cost.
- **This card is the rolled-back-overlayable-type case** — `permission` / `position` / `page` / `app` / `dataset` / `book`, where the maintainer has now ruled the delete direction open because it restores code-declared state and cannot widen anything.

Same argument shape, opposite outcomes, different type sets — which is coherent only if the implementation **scopes the relaxation to the rolled-back overlayable types and leaves the `object` tier refusing exactly as D9 pins it**. That is the design constraint whoever takes this card inherits, and it is the thing most likely to be got wrong by a dev who finds one predicate serving both and relaxes it.

## Dispatch conditions

1. **PR #7306 lands** (it is ACCEPTed, at ready, stopped only behind `ADR maintainer approval`). Dispatching from `main` before then produces a branch with neither D9 nor its pins, and the collision surfaces at landing instead of at authoring.
2. The dispatch will carry, as a hard constraint: **the `object` tier's refusal does not move**; if the two cases cannot be separated without relaxing D9's pinned behaviour, STOP and report rather than editing those pins.
3. The delete-only asymmetry gets recorded in the gate's doc comment per the ruling, so it is not later "fixed" into symmetry — and the save-side comment that already promises repair-must-stay-possible gets extended to name the artifact-backed tier, since that divergence between stated intent and enforced behaviour is what this card opened with.

Zero affected rows today (measured at PR #6608), and the ruling itself says normal priority, not urgent — so the sequencing costs nothing real.

Session: `session_01W6bLax4KMrSfnE1ydFU8Dw`
Branch: `claude/issue-6960-legacy-overlay-delete`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-6960`
Base: `origin/main` @ `f16e54e1d` or later

**The gate this card was held behind has cleared.** PR #7306 (ADR-0029 D9) landed at 09:03:31Z as `f16e54e1d` — verified by unbounded grep on the subject shape plus a single-parent check. The same-function conflict recorded above is therefore resolved in the only way it safely could be: **D9's pins are now on `main`, so the dev branches from a tree that already contains them and any relaxation that disturbs them turns red immediately rather than at landing.**

Dispatching now with the maintainer's 07:36Z ruling as the specification, and the constraint below as the hard boundary.

## The boundary, restated because it is the thing most likely to be got wrong

Two tiers reach the same two refusal points, and only one of them moves:

| tier | what the maintainer ruled | source |
|---|---|---|
| **rolled-back overlayable types** (`permission` / `position` / `page` / `app` / `dataset` / `book`) | **delete is ALLOWED** through the ordinary path — removing an overlay restores code-declared state, is strictly narrowing, and cannot widen anything | this card, 07:36Z |
| **`object`** (overlay write over a packaged object) | **delete stays REFUSED** — D9.6's declared cost, now pinned three times over asserting `code` AND `status` | ADR-0029 D9, landed `f16e54e1d` |

A dev who finds one predicate serving both tiers and relaxes it will turn D9's pins red. **Those pins are correct.** If the two tiers cannot be separated without editing them, that is a **STOP and report**, not a judgement call.

The two refusal points, from this card's own analysis:

- `deleteMetaItem`'s `environmentId !== undefined` branch in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` — `artifactBacked && !overlayAllowed` throws `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403 **before** any probe for the row;
- `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed` refusing `override-artifact` on the no-`environmentId` kernel path (#5086), reached exactly when a row *does* exist because the "no overlay found" probe returns a no-op success earlier. ⚠️ This one is **topology-independent**, so a control-plane kernel refuses too — both paths need the same treatment or the fix is half-done.

## Also ruled, and easy to drop

**Record the delete-only asymmetry in the gate's doc comment**, so it is not later "fixed" into symmetry by someone tidying up. The save-side gate already carries a comment promising that removing a legacy row is repair and must stay possible — but it scopes that carve-out to the **code-only** tier (`allowRuntimeCreate: false` AND `allowOrgOverride: false`), not the artifact-backed tier a rolled-back type now sits in. That divergence between stated intent and enforced behaviour is what this card opened with, so extending that comment to name the artifact-backed tier is part of the deliverable, not a nicety.

**Create and update stay refused exactly as today.** Only delete moves.

## Pricing

Zero affected rows in the corpus today (measured at PR #6608), and the ruling says normal priority, not urgent. So this is a correctness-of-contract change with no live victim — which means the pins are the deliverable and a "it works now" demo is not evidence.

Batch occupancy at dispatch: #7369 in dev, #4717 dispatched alongside this one (region-disjoint — `deleteMetaItem` vs `saveMetaItem`). Three of five.
